subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Should OpenClaw standardize optional ignored `name` metadata for opaque-ID-keyed channel group entries, and which entry schemas are in scope?
rationale: Source proves the usability gap, but heterogeneous channel config shapes cannot determine the permanent public field name or scope without maintainer intent.

options.title: Standardize ID labels
options.body: Add optional ignored `name` to opaque-ID-keyed group and channel entries with one documented contract and aligned validation surfaces.

options.title: Pilot selected channels
options.body: Start with Telegram and other demonstrated opaque-ID cases, leaving name-keyed or structurally different group configs unchanged.

options.title: Keep behavior-only config
options.body: Decline inert metadata and pursue a separate UI-managed or external identifier mapping.

recommendation.title: Standardize ID labels
recommendation.body: Add optional ignored `name` to opaque-ID-keyed group and channel entries with one documented contract and aligned validation surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to strict config policy and repeated maintenance of central channel schema surfaces.
